articles.title: Teenager becomes first person to have testicular tissue transplant in UK
articles.description: Operation on 19-year-old who had no sperm after chemotherapy offers hope of preserving children’s fertility after cancer treatment Surgeons have performed the first testicular tissue transplant on a teenager in the UK, offering hope that boys left infertile by chemotherapy could one day have biological children. The 19-year-old had his tissue removed and frozen three years ago before undergoing treatment for a serious blood disorder. He said he was “incredibly grateful” to the medical team behind the pioneering procedure, which represents a potential breakthrough for male fertility preservation. Continue reading...

articles.title: Margaret Hamilton, trailblazer whose software powered Apollo 11 moon landing, dies at 90
articles.description: MIT computer scientist led development of software for moon mission and earned Presidential Medal of Freedom Margaret Hamilton, the computer pioneer whose software powered the first moon landing, has died, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) announced on Wednesday. She was 90. In an era before titles such as software engineer and computer scientist became mainstream, Hamilton, who died on 30 September, learned to program under the tutelage of a renowned MIT meteorologist. Continue reading...

articles.title: All the news and science from the 2026 Nobel prizes – podcast

source.name: Presented and produced by Madeleine Finlay, with Nicola Davis, Ian Sample and Linda Geddes, sound design by Joel Cox, the executive producer was Ellie Bury

articles.description: This year’s Nobel prizes in chemistry, physics and physiology or medicine have celebrated work that has been used to develop countless drugs and transform modern medicine, allowed physicists to observe one of the most mysterious particles, and provided a tool that could act as an on/off switch for brain cells. To find out more, Madeleine Finlay talks to our science editor, Ian Sample, and correspondents Nicola Davis and Linda Geddes Nobel prize in medicine 2026 awarded for research into mysteries of brain Nobel prize in physics goes to Francis Halzen for south pole work on neutrinos Nobel prize in chemistry awarded for work on mirror-image molecules Continue reading...

articles.title: Moment Karl Deisseroth tells his family he won the Nobel prize in medicine – video
articles.description: Stanford University has shared a video of Karl Deisseroth telling his two daughters and one of his sons he has won a Nobel prize in medicine. Deisseroth spent hours fielding congratulatory calls on Monday after learning he had won the prize for helping to open a field of brain science called optogenetics. articles.title: The generation raised on sugar rations – and what their health reveals 70 years later
articles.description: From blood pressure to ageing, research suggests the first 1,000 days of sugar exposure could leave a decades-long mark on health They were born into a Britain still recovering from the hardships of war. Babies and very young children were expected to have little or no added sugar. Then, in 1953, the brakes came off. Separate restrictions on sweets and chocolate were lifted in February, followed by sugar in September. By the second half of 1954, average sugar consumption had almost doubled. Continue reading...
